text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Greens "amazed" by Finance Minister Sauli Niinisto's arguments in favour of nuclear power and attacks on environment ministry's Natura 2000 programme. Say it shows "basic ignorance" of the diversity of nature.

- Recession and unemployment have not damaged mental health of young Finnish people. However, high-school children seem to have surprisingly many mental problems overall, study by the Social Insurance Institute (KELA) shows.
- State invests about a billion markka in employment training programme, but schemes lack qualified trainers.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Electricity transfer actions should be opened further to competition, Heikki Lehtonen, CEO of Santasalo-Jot says.
- Tightening competition between banking houses may lead to more risk-taking, Financial Supervision Authority warns.
- Today there are many ways to set up closed-circle deals without the authorities finding out, an anonymous bank head says.
- Transport is not able to invest enough and increased demand is not boosting profitability, sector representive says.
- Finnish foundations have underweighted stocks and increased real estate holdings in last couple of years. Only a moderate amount goes to scholarship grants.
AAMULEHTI
- Helsingin Sanomat said it officially supports Finnish membership in EMU -- said Finland should join the union among the first countries.
- Floods of Ounasjoki river damaged large areas of Northern Finland during the weekend.
TURUN SANOMAT

- Finland's EMU membership can be decided with a single majority vote, says Ville Itala, chairman of the Parliament's constitutional committee, basing his arguments on Finland's commitments when signing the Maastricht Treaty.
- Conservative Party's out-of-line policy statements especially on nuclear power hamper government work, says second Finance Minister Arja Alho, criticising Niinisto's remarks in favour.
- Buying army helicopters with Sweden would be a form of fruitful cooperation, Gustav Hagglund, top general says.
- First Finnish rapid deployment troop join Nordic forces to practise in a NATO manoeuvre in Norway this week.
DEMARI
- Helsingin Sanomat's support for EMU has lost Finland's largest newspaper its credibility, says Esko Seppanen, Leftist Alliance's member of European Parliament.
HUFVUDSTADSBLADET
- Drinking alcohol and getting drunk increases by six times the risk of stroke.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
